title: perimeter-telemetry-multiplexer-and-replay-guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated and Private customers experience telemetry spikes and transient network partitions that can cause per-tenant bursts to saturate perimeter collectors, leading to dropped spans, inflated tail latency and noisy error dashboards. On air-gapped/on-prem collectors disk can fill or cause backpressure that affects other tenants.

Goal: Build a perimeter telemetry multiplexer that performs tenant-aware rate-smoothing, short-term durable spooling, and deterministic replay with per-tenant guardrails so we can guarantee no tenant can cause system-wide degradation while preserving trace fidelity for post-incident analysis.

Design summary:
- Perimeter Muxer: lightweight TCP/gRPC front proxy that demultiplexes incoming telemetry streams into tenant shards using identity headers and deterministic hashing. Works in both VPC bridge and on-prem sidecar modes.
- Rate-smoothing: token-bucket per-tenant with adaptive refill based on historical qps and current catalog limits; global admission control enforces soft and hard thresholds.
- Local spool & replay: bounded disk-backed spool per-tenant (configurable size/retention). Under backpressure, oldest non-critical payloads are redacted or sampled according to policy, while high-fidelity traces (sampled by SLO triggers) are pinned for guaranteed replay.
- Replay semantics: signed manifest per spool segment, idempotent replay with sequence checks, per-tenant replay dashboard and guaranteed order preservation within shard.
- Fallback modes: when spool is near capacity, emit aggregated sampled metrics (histogram/approx counts) instead of full traces; allow customer-configured retention vs fidelity tradeoffs.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Spooling reduces data-loss risk but increases disk usage and recovery complexity for on-prem upgrades.
- Deterministic shard routing simplifies replay ordering but may increase hot-spot risk; mitigation via shard-splitting policy.
- Privacy: replay uses tenant keys, all spooled data is encrypted at rest with KMS/HSM key references.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Per-tenant: p95/p99 ingest latency, dropped-span-rate, spool-usage-percent, replay-failures.
- Global: muxer CPU/memory, admission rejections/sec, longest-replay-lag, disk-pressure-alerts.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary in hosted with synthetic tenants (2 weeks) -> collect load profiles.
2) Dedicated beta with one customer using dedicated perimeter (3 weeks) -> iterate configurations.
3) On-prem sidecar pilot with 2 customers (4 weeks) -> focus on spool durability.

Acceptance criteria:
- No increase in global dropped-span-rate under 10x tenant burst compared to baseline.
- Replay preserves >=99% of pinned spans during network partition tests.
- Dashboards show per-tenant spool growth and replay status with <10s refresh latency.
